newsitem.title: GERMANY: Computer 2000 posts loss on Ameriquest woes.
newsitem.headline: Computer 2000 posts loss on Ameriquest woes.

text.p: German computer wholesaler Computer 2000 said on Thursday it made a pre-tax loss of 38 million marks in the first half of its business year which ends on September 30.

The company cited continuing losses at its Ameriquest Technologies Inc unit in the United States, which it said would require further restructuring and cause a group loss for the full year and probably the omission of the dividend.
"Ameriquest is not competitive in the United States with its current structure," Computer 2000 said in statement, adding that restructuring at unit would be "expanded considerably".
"But the goal is to complete the restructuring this year," it said.
Some of the measures to be taken will include closing warehouses, cutting the workforce and selling off some parts of the U.S. company.
Ameriquest would concentrate its activities on the division Advanced Systems Group (ASG), a specialised distributor of high-end workstations and servers.
Computer 2000 group losses in the first half of its business year were attributed largely to operating losses at Ameriquest and transfers to reserves in order to pay for the restructuring programme.

Commenting on the impact of these measures on full year results, the company said: "The board expects another negative result after taxes because of the expanded restructuring programme at Ameriquest and the omission of the dividend."
